scope: Operator-reported noise: 121 'binario engram no encontrado en el PATH del hook' warnings in ~/.engram/sync.log. Root cause found and fixed; verified by running the real hook with a minimal PATH.

who_runs_the_sync.mechanism: The user's own hooks call ~/.engram-sync/sync.sh; engram's cloud is not involved.

correction_of_earlier_reading: Every sync.log line is prefixed with the machine name, not a project name: sync.sh sets HOST="$(hostname -s)" and logs "[HOST] message". The entry '[omarchy] Push OK' therefore means this host (omarchy) pushed its chunk backup, not a project called omarchy. The store's real projects are a different set. An earlier report of mine read that prefix as another project; it is wrong.

cause.code: sync.sh ensure_repo() runs `command -v "$ENGRAM_BIN"` and calls die_soft when the binary is not on the hook's PATH.
cause.evidence: With PATH=~/.local/bin:/usr/bin:/bin, `command -v engram` returned nothing: the binary lives only in /home/linuxbrew/.linuxbrew/bin. The last warning is dated 2026-10-13 12:49, so this was live, not historical.

fix.symlink: /home/iseoane/.local/bin/engram -> /home/linuxbrew/.linuxbrew/bin/engram, created because ~/.local/bin is already first on PATH in the user's login config (~/.zprofile) and is a standard user bin directory for restricted hook environments.
verification: env -i PATH=$HOME/.local/bin:/usr/bin:/bin sh -c 'command -v engram && engram version' -> /home/iseoane/.local/bin/engram, engram 3.4.0
The real hook was executed with that minimal PATH and ENGRAM_LOG pointed at a temporary file: exit 0 and the log shows only 'Import OK' and 'Pull OK', with no PATH warning.
The temporary log was removed; the user's sync.log was not edited by this check.

not_verified: The hook was exercised through `pull` only; `push` was not run by this check.
Whether every possible hook launcher (GUI session, other machines, Windows/PowerShell sync.ps1) inherits a PATH containing ~/.local/bin is untested. sync.ps1 on Windows is untouched.
Three pre-existing real rebase conflicts in the sync log remain unreviewed; they belong to the user's own backup flow and are out of scope here.
limits: Removing the warning does not prove the sync mechanism is correct or that backups are complete; it only shows the hook can now resolve the binary. No memory contents were read, and no engram command was run against another project's selector.
